description: PyPSA-Earth is an open-source global, cross-sectoral energy system model with high spatial and temporal resolution, which its developers describe as the first of its kind. Its workflow can model the energy system of any country in the world for both operational and capacity expansion studies, and its sector-coupled features optimise multi-energy systems covering electricity, heating, transport, industry and hydrogen. All data needed for a simulation are retrieved automatically from open sources, including demand across sectors, generation capacities, medium- to high-voltage networks and renewable energy potentials. It is developed by the PyPSA meets Earth initiative with PyPSA-Eur authors, and its reference paper, led by Maximilian Parzen, demonstrates it in Africa. Code is on GitHub (latest tag v0.9.0), under the GNU Affero GPL version 3 or later at no cost. Caveats: the installation step installs the HiGHS, GLPK and Gurobi solvers, with HiGHS recommended as the open-source choice, while Gurobi is faster but needs a licence, free only for academics. Simulation uses are capacity planning, optimisation and network flow studies in any country. Related records: it builds on model-pypsa and is the global counterpart of model-pypsa-eur.
